content.text:
Reference image 1 shows a lion. Use it only for the head, torso, limbs and skin covering.
Reference image 2 shows a common octopus. Use it only for the tail.
Create one new creature with a single, committed quadruped body plan.
Place the lion's head, torso, limbs and skin covering on the common octopus's frame so every join heals naturally: no visible seams, no floating parts, no duplicated limbs.
no shared habitat: lion forest/grassland/mountain; common octopus marine common octopus lives only in the sea; lion only on land A fusion with a body_plan conflict (e.g. finned x quadruped with no amphibious design note) must be flagged, not silently resolved by picking one parent's plan.
Show the full body in a calm three-quarter view on a plain, softly lit background, in the style of a natural history field-guide plate. Photographic realism, accurate anatomy, no text, no labels, no people.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Fusing lion and octopus**
I'm preparing a reference-to-image fusion that places the lion's head, torso, limbs, and skin onto the octopus's frame, healing all joins for a single quadruped body with no seams or floating parts, in a calm three-quarter view on a plain, softly lit background.
**Rendering hybrid field-guide plate**
I'm creating a natural history-style illustration with a quadruped lion body and a single octopus tentacle as the tail, on a plain background, no text or labels, to visually flag the body-plan conflict.
**Refining natural field-guide style**
I'm adjusting the illustration to feel more natural while keeping the hybrid field-guide plate clear, so the final deliverable reads smoothly and matches what the user wants.
**Generating another bird image**
I'm creating one more bird image to improve on the earlier version with the separate tail, aiming for a cleaner, more natural field-guide look.
